title: Packaging in numbers
heading: How far off is your gut?
intro: Eight real numbers about packaging: how much we throw away, what it's made of, what comes back and the rules that shape the design.
Every figure is real and sourced. Bet on how sure you are.

outro.heading: Packaging is full of trade-offs.
paras: A pack has to protect the product, sell it on a crowded shelf, follow the law and end up somewhere after it's used. Today's numbers showed how far apart our guesses and the real picture can be.
Bring that habit with you: when the team argues about a pack, ask what the evidence actually says.

questions.q: How much packaging waste did the average person in the EU produce in 2023?
questions.explain: That's almost half a kilo a day for every person: 79.7 million tonnes across the EU. It was 8.7 kg less than in 2022, but 21.2 kg more than in 2013.

questions.q: Which material makes up the largest share of the EU's packaging waste?
questions.explain: Paper and cardboard make up 40.4% of EU packaging waste, about twice as much as plastic (19.8%) and glass (18.8%). Online shopping boxes are part of the reason.

questions.q: Germany puts a 25-cent deposit (Pfand) on most single-use drinks bottles and cans. What share of them come back?
questions.explain: Between 96 and 99% of single-use deposit bottles and cans are returned, depending on the source. The deposit started in 2003, and the logo on the label tells you a bottle is worth money.
questions.source: Umweltbundesamt, 2026 (via Euronews); DPG Deutsche Pfandsystem GmbH

questions.q: Scotland planned a 20p deposit on drinks containers, first due to start in 2022. When are UK deposit schemes now due to start?
questions.explain: Scotland's scheme was delayed several times; in 2023 the UK government allowed it only without glass, and the company set up to run it went into administration. All four UK nations now plan to start on 1 October 2027; only Wales will include glass.
questions.source: Clarity, UK Deposit Return Scheme: Where Are We Now?, September 2026; Senedd Research, Deposit return scheme regulations in brief, 2026

questions.q: In 2023 Toblerone took the Matterhorn mountain off some of its packs. Why?
options: Swiss rules: bars made partly in Slovakia can't use Swiss symbols
A copyright dispute with the town of Zermatt
To save ink and printing costs
questions.explain: Under Switzerland's 'Swissness' law, a food can only use Swiss symbols if at least 80% of its raw materials are Swiss and its key processing happens in Switzerland. With some production moving to Bratislava, the Matterhorn was replaced by a simpler mountain logo.

questions.q: What share of the plastic made for the European market goes into packaging?
questions.sub: the largest single use of plastic
questions.explain: Packaging made up about 39% of plastics demand in Europe in 2021, far more than building and construction (about 21%) or cars (about 9%). Much of it is designed to be used only once.
questions.source: European Environment Agency, Nearly 40 percent of plastic demand comes from packaging, 2023 (Plastics Europe data for 2021)

questions.q: Where on a glass bottle of Heinz ketchup does Heinz say you should tap to get the ketchup out?
options: On the side of the label
questions.explain: A Heinz spokesperson said the sweet spot is the embossed '57' on the neck: give it a firm tap where the bottle narrows. The design hides a user instruction in plain sight that many people never notice.
questions.source: Heinz spokesperson, reported by Shortlist and Refinery29, 2016

questions.q: Since 2022 UK firms have paid tax on plastic packaging that contains less than 30% recycled plastic. From April 2026, roughly how much per tonne?
questions.explain: The rate rose from £223.69 to £228.82 per tonne in April 2026. It's small per pack, but large across millions of packs, and it pushes firms towards recycled plastic.
questions.source: HM Revenue & Customs, Plastic Packaging Tax rates (reported by Rödl & Partner, March 2026)
